title: Listen back
summary: Record a run-through, listen to it twice, and fix the one thing you could not hear while playing.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

steps.title: Listen back
steps.body:
You cannot hear yourself properly while you play. Your ears are busy, your hands are busy, and your brain is busy telling the hands what comes next. The recording hears what you cannot.

1. Record one run-through of the piece on the phone. Audio is enough.
2. Listen to it once without doing anything. Then listen again with the page in front of you and a pencil.
3. Mark the one thing you would fix first. One, not five. An uneven beat, a rushed bar, a note held too short.
4. Practise that one thing, slowly, then record again and listen for it.

Listening back is how every musician improves after the lesson ends. The teacher hears you once a week; the phone can hear you every day.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: record a run-through, listen twice, mark one thing to fix
Sitting 2: practise that one thing slowly, record again, listen for it
Sitting 3: a new recording, a new single thing to fix
Sitting 4: the whole piece once through, then listen back one last time
An old piece recorded and listened to once; what did you hear?

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play it once through, hands in the frame. Slips stay in.
